the_number_this_leg_adds.why_it_matters: k(r) indexes BCG's solution branches (k(r_j) = j).  k(7/6) = 16.3479 therefore says EXACTLY which branches lie on which side of the dominance boundary -- a question neither BCG nor CGSS nor any prior leg answers, because BCG only ever say 'n odd and large enough' and never quantify it.

CORRECTION_TO_LEG_251.leg_251_ansatz_wording: r^(n) in (r_n(gamma), r_{n+1}(gamma)), n odd and LARGE
CORRECTION_TO_LEG_251.the_incompatibility: k is monotone increasing to +infinity at r*, so LARGE n forces r -> r*, i.e. DEEP INSIDE BCG's dominance window -- exactly where the existing theorem already works and where obligation 4 (r-coverage outside the dominance regime) is violated.  Leg 251's named ansatz and its own obligation 4 pull in OPPOSITE directions.
CORRECTION_TO_LEG_251.the_repair: the certificate's ansatz must take SMALL odd n, n <= 15.
CORRECTION_TO_LEG_251.this_is_a_measurement_not_an_opinion: n >= 17 is forced for BCG's own NS theorem by r_n >= 7/6.

the_recommended_construction_target.why: BCG Thm 1.1 (l.214) gives r^(3) for ALL gamma > 1 UNCONDITIONALLY -- existence is not contingent on any 'large enough'.  It is the only branch in the target window whose profile is guaranteed to exist.
the_recommended_construction_target.cost_of_choosing_it: |delta_dis| ~ 0.43-0.58, i.e. the dissipative forcing GROWS like e^{+0.5 s}, against an architecture calibrated for decay at rate <= 0.146.

the_cheapest_target_if_existence_can_be_.why: the odd branch closest below the borderline: |delta_dis| <= 0.0141, about 31-41x smaller than the n=3 branch's, so the forcing's growth rate is minimal.
the_cheapest_target_if_existence_can_be_.UNRESOLVED: BCG Thm 1.2 requires 'n odd and large ENOUGH' for gamma = 7/5 and NEVER QUANTIFIES IT.  Whether n = 15 qualifies is not stated in the paper and is NOT settled here.  Reported as open, not assumed either way.

the_autonomous_point.fact: delta_dis = 0, so F_dis's prefactor is s-INDEPENDENT and the dissipative self-similar system is AUTONOMOUS -- the one exponent at which a stationary viscous profile problem exists at all.
the_autonomous_point.but: k(7/6) = 16.3479 is not an integer, so 7/6 lies in the gap (r_16, r_17), which is an EVEN index.  BCG's shooting argument uses n ODD (their footnote at l.373: 'The requirement that n is odd is used to ensure (pt:1)').  So BCG's construction supplies NO profile at the one exponent where the object would be stationary.

deliverable_1_the_term.question: the profile equation and the precise term to enclose, from BCG/CGSS full text

stationary_profile_system.what: the EULER self-similar system -- dissipation does NOT enter it
stationary_profile_system.bcg_locator: arXiv:2208.09445 (eq:DS); Thm 1.2 l.217 produces a solution of it, Thm 1.3 l.220 opens 'Let (U^E,S^E) be the profiles of Theorem 1.2, solving (eq:DS)' -- superscript E for Euler
stationary_profile_system.cgss_locator: arXiv:2310.05325 (eq:ss_profiles) l.319-322, written out for nu=0: (r-1)Ubar + (y+Ubar).grad Ubar + alpha Sbar grad Sbar = 0, (r-1)Sbar + (y+Ubar).grad Sbar + alpha Sbar div(Ubar) = 0
stationary_profile_system.confirms: leg 266's re-posing, independently and from a SECOND paper

the_term_to_enclose.name: F_dis, 'the dissipative forcing' (BCG's own words, l.2142)
the_term_to_enclose.enters_at: BCG l.2138-2139, the RIGHT-HAND SIDES of the dynamically rescaled (Wtilde,Ztilde) system (eq:tildeWZ:def2), added to the nonlinear forcing
the_term_to_enclose.cgss_independent_form_l382: nu C_dis e^{-delta_dis s} Delta U / S^{1/alpha}
the_term_to_enclose.structure: LOCAL.  A second-order differential operator on U, divided by a positive power of the sound speed S.  No nonlocal operator anywhere -- see deliverable 2's census.

top_order_energy_term.form: J = int (r^(1+1/alpha)/alpha^(1/alpha)) e^{-delta_dis s} Delta^K (Delta U / S^(1/alpha)) Delta^K U phi^(2K)
top_order_energy_term.bcg_own_words_l3804: 'we treat the term coming from the dissipation, which one cannot expect to bound (since it has more derivatives than our energy).  Thus, the strategy is to extract the correct sign for this term.'
top_order_energy_term.how_bcg_close_it: NOT by bounding it.  By integration by parts they show |(alpha^(1/alpha)/r^(1+1/alpha)) e^{delta_dis s} J + G^2| <~ G, where G^2 = sum_i int (grad Delta^K U_i)^2 / S^(1/alpha) phi^(2K) >= 0 (l.3945).  So J is DOMINATED BY -G^2: the dissipative term enters the top-order energy with a FAVOURABLE SIGN and is never bounded, only signed.

stable_projection_forcing_bound.form: ||F_dis(.,s)||_X <= delta_1 e^{-delta_dis s/2} <= delta_1^{3/2} e^{-(9/10) delta_g (s-s0)}
stable_projection_forcing_bound.why_it_matters: this is the load-bearing inequality of the whole stability step: it converts the dissipative forcing's decay rate delta_dis/2 into a rate strictly faster than the semigroup's spectral gap (9/10)delta_g, which is what makes the Duhamel integral at l.4078 converge (int e^{-delta_g(s-sbar)/2 - (9/10)delta_g(sbar-s0)} dsbar).

parameter_hierarchy.bcg_locator: l.2994, 'For the convenience of the reader, we collect the following chain of inequalities'
parameter_hierarchy.chain_verbatim: 1/s0 << delta_0^{3/2} << delta_1 << delta_g delta_0 << delta_0 << 1/Ebar << 1/K << 1/m << eta_w << delta_g << delta_dis = O(1)
parameter_hierarchy.consequence: the obligation asks for r with delta_dis <= 0.  That does not violate one inequality -- it removes the TOP element of an 11-element ordered chain that the other 10 are calibrated against.

what_inverts.at_positive_delta_dis: every dissipative bound carries e^{-delta_dis s0/2}, and 's0 sufficiently large' MAKES IT SMALL
what_inverts.at_nonpositive_delta_dis: the same factor is e^{+|delta_dis| s0/2}: taking s0 large -- the proof's only smallness knob -- makes it LARGE.  The monotonicity in the free parameter flips sign.

what_inverts.item: the Duhamel convergence in the stable projection
what_inverts.at_positive_delta_dis: int_{s0}^{s} e^{-delta_g(s-sbar)/2} ||F_dis(sbar)||_X dsbar converges because 9/10 delta_g > 1/2 delta_g
what_inverts.at_nonpositive_delta_dis: ||F_dis||_X grows like e^{|delta_dis|sbar/2}, so the integral behaves like e^{+|delta_dis|s/2} and DIVERGES.  The bootstrap estimate (eq:maracas3) fails outright.
what_inverts.severity: the estimate is false, not merely unproved

what_inverts.at_nonpositive_delta_dis: STILL <= 0 -- e^{-delta_dis s} > 0 for every real delta_dis, so the leading term is negative regardless, and its magnitude GROWS.  Viscosity is stabilising at top order at every r.
what_inverts.severity: SURVIVES.  This is the certificate's structural asset, and it is the reason the obligation is statable at all rather than absurd.

E_2K_top_order_energy.character: ALGEBRAICALLY weighted (phi), on the whole space, at derivative order 2K >> 2m

leg_257_analogue_check.leg_257_mechanism: P[(U.grad)U] has an algebraic |x|^-4 tail whose coefficient is int|U|^2 > 0, so it leaves L^2(mu) for ANY nonzero div-free U in H^2(mu); F is not even well-defined.  Fitted exponent -3.000000 for v, multipole ratio 1.000000 at r=10/20/40/80.
two_things_that_mechanism_requires: a NONLOCAL operator, to manufacture an algebraic tail from a decaying input
a weight growing faster than every algebraic rate (Gaussian), for the tail to defeat
leg_257_analogue_check.requirement_1_verdict: ABSENT, AND MEASURED.  15 of 16 nonlocal probe terms are 0 in both papers against live controls of 167 (BCG) and 185 (CGSS); the 16th ('vorticity', 5 and 5) was adjudicated line by line and is 0 in either paper's own mathematics.  Compressible NS has no Leray projector because its pressure is the CONSTITUTIVE p(rho)=rho^gamma/gamma.
leg_257_analogue_check.requirement_2_verdict: ABSENT.  BCG's weights are unweighted-on-a-ball and algebraic; an algebraic tail against an algebraic weight is a finite exponent budget, not an infinite one.
leg_257_analogue_check.leg_261_discriminator: leg 261 measured the boundary of leg 257's mechanism as 'whether the nonlocal output stands alone or is multiplied by a localised factor'.  Here there is no nonlocal output at all, so the discriminator is not even reached.

BUT_A_DIFFERENT_OBSTRUCTION_OF_THE_SAME_.statement: leg 257's finding is, in type, 'the operator that makes the model a fluid is not defined on the space the argument runs in'.  The compressible imploding problem HAS an obstruction of that exact type, and this leg names it rather than reporting a clean absence.

obstruction_A_derivative_excess.what: D_dis : (U,S) -> Delta U / S^{1/alpha} costs TWO derivatives.  X = H^{2m}(B(0,2)) controls 2m; D_dis maps H^{2m} -> H^{2m-2}, so it is NOT a bounded operator X -> X.  In the top-order energy the same: the estimate needs |grad^{i+2} U| for i+j = 2m, i.e. up to grad^{2m+2}.
obstruction_A_derivative_excess.named_by_the_authors: BCG l.3804 'one cannot expect to bound (since it has more derivatives than our energy)'; CGSS l.494 'we will use weighted energy estimates at a higher derivative level than the linear stability (regularity higher than m)'
obstruction_A_derivative_excess.severity_vs_leg_257: NOT FATAL.  Leg 257's obstruction admits no repair -- int r^{-8} e^{r^2/4} r^2 dr = +infinity, an infinite margin.  This one is repaired by SIGN EXTRACTION, available because D_dis is parabolic and negative-definite while P[(U.grad)U] has no sign.
obstruction_A_derivative_excess.does_the_repair_survive_the_obligation: YES.  The sign of -e^{-delta_dis s}G^2 is independent of delta_dis.

obstruction_B_vacuum_degeneracy.what: the multiplier S^{-1/alpha}, with 1/alpha = 2/(gamma-1) = 5 at gamma = 7/5: a fifth-order pole at the vacuum S -> 0
obstruction_B_vacuum_degeneracy.how_bcg_control_it: S(zeta) > Sbar(zeta) - delta_1 >~ 1 for zeta < 6/5 (l.3608), and S<zeta>^{r-1} <~ 1 in the far field (Lemma:suecia)
obstruction_B_vacuum_degeneracy.named_by_the_authors: CGSS l.494, 'together with lower bounds for S to rule out possible vacuum'
obstruction_B_vacuum_degeneracy.severity: a genuine singular multiplier whose ORDER DIVERGES as gamma -> 1; at gamma = 7/5 it is 5, and it is delta_dis-independent, so it neither worsens nor improves inside the target window

deliverable_4_gap_to_clay.question: the honest gap between 'certificate for the compressible imploding profile' and Clay's incompressible problem

gap.item: the equation is not Clay's equation
gap.detail: Clay asks about 3D INCOMPRESSIBLE Navier-Stokes: div u = 0, a NONLOCAL pressure determined by an elliptic problem.  The target is 3D isentropic COMPRESSIBLE Navier-Stokes with the CONSTITUTIVE pressure p(rho) = rho^gamma/gamma.  These differ in the operator that makes the Clay problem hard.
gap.irony_worth_stating: the very absence that makes leg 257's obstruction inapplicable here -- no Leray projector -- is the same absence that makes this object not Clay's object.  The two facts are one fact.

gap.item: the blow-up mechanism is not the Clay mechanism
gap.detail: implosion is driven by compression of the density; the Clay problem's danger is vortex stretching.  Radially, this profile carries NO vorticity-stretching mechanism at all (leg 251 section 3).

3D-ness comes from a spherically-symmetric ODE profile; the certificate would enclose a 1D ODE system in the self-similar variable.  Same side of the line as every existing work (leg 251, re-affirmed here).

BCG Thm 1.3 already PROVES finite-time implosion for compressible NS.  A certificate would upgrade the viscous term's treatment from DOMINATED to ENCLOSED (leg 174/240's grading) at exponents the existing theorem cannot reach.  It would not decide a question currently open in the yes/no sense.
